title: The Teachings of the Apostles
content:
The Teachings of the Apostles

Read Instructions · Instructions index · Beyond the Torah · Counting and classification guide

These 124 records are teachings, including doctrine and promises as well as instructions. They are not a verified count of 124 distinct commands. Find every existing teaching in the coordinated index.

Acts and the apostolic letters · 124 total teachings · 68 major teachings, each with the word of Christ it carries · 56 minor teachings, each with the Scripture or event it rests on

The teachings are set out in two orders. The major teachings are those in which the apostles hand on a word of the Lord Himself: each is followed by the commandment of Christ it carries, linked to The Commandments of Christ or to the Gospel passage. The minor teachings rest on Christ less directly. They are drawn from the Law, the Prophets, the Psalms and the events of sacred history, read in the light of Christ: each is followed by the verses or events the apostle points to, linked to their place in the Saints Translation. “Minor” is a description of how a teaching is grounded, not of its weight.

Each entry gives the teaching in a sentence of our own, then the cited source’s words from the Saints Translation (long passages are shortened, with a link to the whole), then other places where the same is taught. The selection and the grouping are an editor’s gathering for study, not a complete catalogue. Psalms are numbered as in the Saints Translation, with the Hebrew number in parentheses. At the foot of the page is an index by book.

Major teachings: The Gospel Proclaimed · Love, the Fulfilling of the Law · Enemies, Vengeance and Forgiveness · Humility and Service · Speech and the Heart · Prayer · Riches and Generosity · Marriage · Rulers and the Obedience Owed to God · Suffering with Christ · Watchfulness and the Day of the Lord · Light, Worship and the World

Minor teachings: The Faith of the Fathers · Adam, the Promise and the Law · Warnings from Israel’s History · Christ in the Law and the Prophets · Wisdom for the Household of God

Major Teachings: The Word of Christ Handed On

The Gospel Proclaimed

1. To repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and to receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

Peter said to them, “Repent, and let each one of you be baptized upon the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is for you, for your children, and for all who are far away—as many as the Lord our God calls to Himself.”

Acts 2:38–39

Also taught in: Acts 3:19
The word of Christ: To repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near · To go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father…

2. To bear witness to Him to the end of the earth; He commanded us to proclaim that everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.

He commanded us to proclaim to the people and bear solemn witness that He is the One appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead. All the prophets bear witness to Him: everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.”

Acts 10:42–43

Also taught in: Acts 1:8 · Acts 13:38–39
The word of Christ: That repentance and forgiveness of sins be proclaimed in His name to all the nations…

3. There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved.

Salvation is in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among human beings by which we must be saved.”

Acts 4:12

The word of Christ: John 14:6

4. To believe in the Lord Jesus; to confess with the mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in the heart that God raised Him.

Because if you confess Jesus as Lord with your mouth, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved; for with the heart one believes for righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses for salvation.

Romans 10:9–10

Also taught in: Acts 16:31
The word of Christ: This is the work of God: to believe in the One He sent · To acknowledge Him before people

5. To be born anew, not of perishable seed but through the living and abiding word of God.

having been born anew, not from perishable seed but from imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God.

1 Peter 1:23

Also taught in: Titus 3:5 · James 1:18
The word of Christ: You must be born from above, of water and Spirit

6. To be buried with Him through baptism into death, and to walk in newness of life.

Or do you not know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death? Therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the Father’s glory, so we also might walk in newness of life.

Romans 6:3–4

Also taught in: Colossians 2:12 · Galatians 3:27
The word of Christ: To go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father… · To deny yourself, take up your cross, and follow Him

7. To keep the Supper as received from the Lord: this is My body, this cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this in remembrance of Me.

For I received from the Lord what I also handed over to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when He was being handed over, took bread, and after giving thanks He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.” Likewise He also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of Me.” For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.

1 Corinthians 11:23–26

Also taught in: 1 Corinthians 10:16–17
The word of Christ: To take and eat: this is His body; to drink of the cup: this is His blood of the…

8. To remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

In everything I showed you that by working in this way we must support the weak and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”

Acts 20:35

The word of Christ: To proclaim that the kingdom has drawn near, to heal the sick; freely you received… · To love your enemies, do good, and lend expecting nothing back

Love, the Fulfilling of the Law

9. To owe no one anything except to love one another: the commandments are summed up in this word, You shall love your neighbor as yourself.

Owe no one anything except to love one another; for the one who loves the other has fulfilled law. For “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” Love does not work evil toward the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.

Romans 13:8–10

The word of Christ: The second, like it: to love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments hang… · If you wish to enter life, keep the commandments: you shall not murder, commit…

10. The whole Law is fulfilled in one word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.

For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not make freedom a base of operations for the flesh, but through love serve one another as slaves. For the whole law is fulfilled in one saying: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

Galatians 5:13–14

The word of Christ: The second, like it: to love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments hang…

11. To fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, You shall love your neighbor as yourself.

If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.

James 2:8

The word of Christ: The second, like it: to love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments hang…

12. This is His commandment: to believe in the name of His Son Jesus Christ and to love one another, just as He commanded us.

And this is His commandment: that we believe in the name of His Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as He gave us a commandment.

1 John 3:23

Also taught in: 1 John 4:21 · 2 John 1:5–6 · 1 John 4:7–11
The word of Christ: A new commandment: to love one another as He has loved you · This is the work of God: to believe in the One He sent

13. By this we know that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments and walk as He walked.

And by this we know that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments. The one who says, “I have come to know Him,” and does not keep His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in that person. But whoever keeps His word, in that person the love of God has truly been brought to completion. By this we know that we are in Him. The one who says that he abides in Him ought himself also to walk just as He walked.

1 John 2:3–6

Also taught in: 1 John 5:3
The word of Christ: If you love Me, keep My commandments · To remain in Him and in His love

14. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer.

Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.

1 John 3:15

Also taught in: 1 John 2:9–11
The word of Christ: Murder: whoever is angry with his brother, insults him or calls him a fool is liable to…

15. Not to love in word or tongue but in deed and truth: whoever sees his brother in need and closes his heart, how does the love of God remain in him?.

But whoever has this world’s means of living and sees his brother in need and closes his heart against him, how does the love of God abide in him? Little children, let us not love in word or with the tongue, but in deed and truth.

1 John 3:17–18

Also taught in: James 2:15–16
The word of Christ: What you did to one of the least of these His brothers, you did to Him · Go, and do likewise: to show mercy as the Samaritan did

16. Love is patient and kind; it bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

Love is patient; love is kind. Love is not jealous, does not boast, is not puffed up, does not behave shamefully, does not seek its own interests, is not provoked, does not keep account of wrong, does not rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth. It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

1 Corinthians 13:4–7

Also taught in: Colossians 3:14 · 1 Peter 4:8
The word of Christ: A new commandment: to love one another as He has loved you

Enemies, Vengeance and Forgiveness

17. To bless those who persecute you; to repay no one evil for evil; to overcome evil with good.

Bless those who persecute; bless, and do not curse. … Repay no one evil for evil. Take thought for what is honorable before all people. If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people. Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.” But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head. Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.

Romans 12:14 · Romans 12:17–21

The word of Christ: Love of neighbor: to love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so as to… · An eye for an eye: not to resist the evil person; to turn the other cheek, give the…

18. Not to return evil for evil or insult for insult, but to bless.

not repaying evil for evil or reviling for reviling, but, on the contrary, blessing, because you were called for this, so that you might inherit a blessing.

1 Peter 3:9

Also taught in: 1 Thessalonians 5:15
The word of Christ: Love of neighbor: to love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so as to… · An eye for an eye: not to resist the evil person; to turn the other cheek, give the…

19. To forgive one another, just as the Lord forgave you.

Therefore put on, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, tender compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience, bearing with one another and forgiving one another if anyone has a complaint against someone. Just as the Lord forgave you, so also must you.

Colossians 3:12–13

Also taught in: Ephesians 4:32
The word of Christ: To forgive, so that your Father may forgive you · To forgive your brother not seven times but seventy times seven

20. Not to let the sun go down on your anger; to put away all bitterness, wrath and slander.

Be angry and do not sin. Do not let the sun go down upon your anger, nor give a place to the devil. … Let all bitterness and rage and anger and shouting and slander be taken away from you, with all malice.

Ephesians 4:26–27 · Ephesians 4:31

The word of Christ: Murder: whoever is angry with his brother, insults him or calls him a fool is liable to…

21. To restore in a spirit of gentleness the one caught in a trespass, and to bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.

Brothers, even if a person is overtaken in some transgression, you who are spiritual are to restore such a person in a spirit of gentleness, watching yourself, lest you too be tempted. Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.

Galatians 6:1–2

Also taught in: James 5:19–20
The word of Christ: If your brother sins, to show him his fault between you and him alone; then with one or…

22. Not to judge your brother or despise him, for we shall all stand before the judgment seat of God.

But why do you judge your brother? Or you also, why do you despise your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat, for it is written, “As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bend to Me, and every tongue will confess to God.” So each of us will give an account concerning himself. Therefore let us no longer judge one another; but judge this instead: not to place a stumbling block or a snare for a brother.

Romans 14:10–13

Also taught in: James 4:11–12
The word of Christ: Not to judge, so that you are not judged; first to take the beam out of your own eye

23. Judgment is without mercy to the one who has shown no mercy; mercy triumphs over judgment.

For judgment is without mercy to the one who has shown no mercy; mercy triumphs over judgment.

James 2:13

The word of Christ: To be merciful, as your Father is merciful · Not to judge, so that you are not judged; first to take the beam out of your own eye

Humility and Service

24. To have the mind of Christ Jesus, who emptied Himself, taking the form of a slave; to count others above yourselves.

doing nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility considering one another above yourselves, each looking not to your own interests, but each also to those of others. Have this mind among yourselves which was also in Christ Jesus, who, existing in the form of God, did not regard being equal with God as something to exploit, but emptied Himself, taking the form of a slave, coming to be in the likeness of human beings; and being found in appearance as a human being, He humbled Himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross.

Philippians 2:3–8

The word of Christ: Whoever wishes to be great among you shall be your servant, as the Son of Man came to… · To wash one another’s feet, as He has done

25. To clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, and to humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God.

Likewise, you who are younger, submit yourselves to the elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” Therefore, humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, so that He may exalt you in due time,

1 Peter 5:5–6

Also taught in: James 4:10
The word of Christ: To take the last place, for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled

26. Elders are to shepherd the flock of God willingly, not lording it over those in their charge but being examples.

Therefore, I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a participant in the glory about to be revealed: Shepherd the flock of God among you, exercising oversight, not under compulsion but willingly, according to God; not for shameful gain but eagerly; not as lording it over those allotted to you, but becoming examples to the flock. And when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.

1 Peter 5:1–4

Also taught in: Acts 20:28
The word of Christ: To feed His lambs and shepherd His sheep · Whoever wishes to be great among you shall be your servant, as the Son of Man came to…

27. Not to put a stumbling block in a brother’s way; not to destroy by your food the one for whom Christ died.

Therefore let us no longer judge one another; but judge this instead: not to place a stumbling block or a snare for a brother. I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself; except that to the one who reckons something unclean, to that person it is unclean. For if your brother is grieved because of food, you no longer walk according to love. Do not destroy with your food the one for whom Christ died.

Romans 14:13–15

Also taught in: 1 Corinthians 8:9–13
The word of Christ: Not to despise one of these little ones, nor cause one of them to stumble

28. To show no partiality: not to give the rich man the good seat and tell the poor man to stand.

My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with acts of favoritism. For if a man with gold rings and splendid clothing enters your gathering, and a poor person in filthy clothing also enters, and you attend to the one wearing splendid clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” but say to the poor person, “You stand, or sit there beneath my footstool,” have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts? Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen those poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?

James 2:1–5

The word of Christ: When you give a feast, to invite the poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind · To take the last place, for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled

29. To receive the runaway slave no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother, as you would receive the apostle himself.

For perhaps he was separated from you for a little while for this reason: that you might have him back forever, no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord. So if you regard me as a partner, welcome him as you would me.

Philemon 1:15–17

The word of Christ: Not to be called Rabbi, father or guide, for you are all brothers · Whoever wishes to be great among you shall be your servant, as the Son of Man came to…

30. To receive and send on their way the brothers who went out for the sake of the Name, and so to become fellow workers for the truth.

Beloved, you act faithfully in whatever you do for the brothers, even though they are strangers, who have borne witness to your love before the Church. You will do well to send them onward in a manner worthy of God, for they went out for the sake of the Name, receiving nothing from the Gentiles. We therefore ought to support such people, so that we may become fellow workers with the truth.

3 John 1:5–8

Also taught in: 3 John 1:11
The word of Christ: To take nothing for the road, to remain in one house, and to shake off the dust where… · Matthew 10:40–42

Speech and the Heart

31. Above all, not to swear, by heaven or by earth or by any other oath; let your Yes be yes and your No be no.

But above all, my brothers, do not swear, either by heaven or by earth or by any other oath. Let your yes be yes, and your no be no, so that you may not fall under judgment.

James 5:12

The word of Christ: Oaths: not to swear at all; let your word be Yes, yes, or No, no

32. To be doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.

But become doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves. For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror, for he looked at himself and went away and immediately forgot what he was like. But the one who looks closely into the complete law, the law of freedom, and continues in it, becoming no forgetful hearer but a doer of work, will be blessed in his doing.

James 1:22–25

The word of Christ: To hear His words and do them, like the man who built upon the rock

33. Nothing is unclean in itself; the kingdom of God is not food and drink but righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.

I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself; except that to the one who reckons something unclean, to that person it is unclean. … For God’s kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit;

Romans 14:14 · Romans 14:17

Also taught in: Acts 10:15
The word of Christ: Nothing that goes into a person from outside can defile him; what comes out of the…

34. Blessing and cursing come out of the same mouth; this ought not to be. Can a fig tree bear olives?.

With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings who have been made in God’s likeness. From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to happen this way. Does a spring pour out sweet and bitter water from the same opening? My brothers, can a fig tree produce olives, or a vine figs? Neither can salt water produce sweet water.

James 3:9–12

The word of Christ: To beware of false prophets, who come in sheep’s clothing · Matthew 12:34–37

35. To put away falsehood and speak truth; to let no rotten word come out of your mouth, but what builds up.

Therefore, putting away falsehood, let each speak truth with his neighbor, because we are members of one another. … Let no rotten word come out of your mouth, but only what is good for building up as needed, so that it may give grace to those who hear.

Ephesians 4:25 · Ephesians 4:29

Also taught in: Colossians 4:6
The word of Christ: Matthew 12:36–37

Prayer

36. To rejoice always, pray without ceasing, and give thanks in everything.

Rejoice always. Pray unceasingly. Give thanks in everything, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.

1 Thessalonians 5:16–18

Also taught in: Colossians 4:2 · Ephesians 6:18
The word of Christ: Always to pray and not lose heart

37. If anyone lacks wisdom, to ask God, who gives generously; but to ask in faith, doubting nothing.

But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to all generously and without reproach, and it will be given to him. But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind. For that person must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord, a man of divided mind, unstable in all his ways.

James 1:5–8

The word of Christ: To ask, to seek, to knock · To have faith in God: to believe that you have received what you ask

38. Not to be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and petition with thanksgiving to make your requests known to God.

Be anxious about nothing, but in everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses every understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

Philippians 4:6–7

The word of Christ: Not to be anxious for your life, what you will eat or wear

39. To cast all your anxiety upon Him, because He cares for you.

casting all your anxiety upon Him, because He cares for you.

1 Peter 5:7

The word of Christ: Not to be anxious for your life, what you will eat or wear

40. This is the confidence we have toward Him: if we ask anything according to His will, He hears us.

And this is the confidence we have toward Him: if we ask anything according to His will, He hears us. And if we know that He hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests we have asked of Him.

1 John 5:14–15

Also taught in: 1 John 3:21–22
The word of Christ: To ask the Father in His name

41. You received a Spirit of adoption, in whom we cry, Abba, Father.

For all who are led by God’s Spirit are sons of God. For you did not receive a spirit of slavery again for fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption as sons, in whom we cry, “Abba, Father.” The Spirit Himself bears witness with our spirit that we are God’s children.

Romans 8:14–16

Also taught in: Galatians 4:6
The word of Christ: The prayer He gave: Our Father

42. Is anyone among you sick? Let him call the elders of the church to pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord; confess your sins to one another.

Is anyone among you sick? Let him summon the elders of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the Lord’s name. And the prayer of faith will save the weary sick person, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he has committed sins, he will be forgiven. Therefore confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. A righteous person’s petition has great strength when it is at work.

James 5:14–16

The word of Christ: As the Father has sent Me, I also send you. Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you… · Mark 6:12–13

Riches and Generosity

43. Godliness with contentment is great gain; the love of money is a root of all evils.

But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into the world, because neither can we carry anything out. But having food and coverings, with these we will be content. But those who want to become rich fall into temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful desires, which plunge human beings into ruin and destruction. For the love of money is a root of all evils, and some, reaching for it, wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many pains.

1 Timothy 6:6–10

Also taught in: Hebrews 13:5
The word of Christ: You cannot serve God and mammon · To guard against all greed, for life is not in the abundance of possessions

44. The rich are not to set their hope on uncertain riches but to be rich in good works, storing up a good foundation for the future.

Command those who are rich in the present age not to be high-minded nor to set their hope on the uncertainty of wealth, but on God, who richly provides us all things for enjoyment, to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous, ready to share, storing up for themselves a good foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of the life that is truly life.

1 Timothy 6:17–19

The word of Christ: Not to store up treasures on earth, but in heaven

45. Come now, you rich: your gold and silver have rusted; the wages you withheld from the workers cry out.

Come now, you rich people: weep and howl over the miseries coming upon you. Your riches have rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten. Your gold and silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be a testimony against you and will devour your flesh. You have stored up treasure like fire in the last days. Look, the wages of the laborers who reaped your fields, withheld by you, cry out; and the cries of the harvesters have entered the ears of the Lord Sabaoth. You lived luxuriously on the earth and indulged yourselves; you fattened your hearts on a day of slaughter.

James 5:1–5

The word of Christ: Not to store up treasures on earth, but in heaven · Luke 6:24–25

46. Each is to give as he has decided in his heart, not grudgingly, for God loves a cheerful giver.

Now this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows in blessings will also reap in blessings. Let each give as he has decided in his heart, not out of sorrow or compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.

2 Corinthians 9:6–7

The word of Christ: To give alms in secret

47. The Lord directed that those who proclaim the good news should live from the good news; the worker is worthy of his wages.

In the same way, the Lord directed those who proclaim the good news to live from the good news.

1 Corinthians 9:14

Also taught in: 1 Timothy 5:18
The word of Christ: To take nothing for the road, to remain in one house, and to shake off the dust where… · Luke 10:7

Marriage

48. To the married I command, not I but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband, and a husband is not to divorce his wife.

To the married I give this instruction—not I, but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband— but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband—and a husband is not to dismiss his wife.

1 Corinthians 7:10–11

The word of Christ: Divorce: whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, makes her commit… · What God has yoked together, no human being is to separate. Moses permitted divorce…

49. Husbands are to love their wives as Christ loved the church; the two shall become one flesh.

Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the Church and gave Himself for her, … “For this reason a man will leave father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.” This mystery is great, but I am speaking with reference to Christ and the Church. Nevertheless, let each one of you also love his own wife as himself, and let the wife respect her husband.

Ephesians 5:25 · Ephesians 5:31–33

Also taught in: Colossians 3:19
The word of Christ: What God has yoked together, no human being is to separate. Moses permitted divorce…

Rulers and the Obedience Owed to God

50. To be subject to the governing authorities and to pay to all what is owed: tax to whom tax, honor to whom honor.

Let every soul submit to the higher authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been appointed by God. … For this reason you also pay taxes, for they are God’s ministers, persisting in this very task. Pay everyone what is owed: tax to whom tax, duty to whom duty, fear to whom fear, honor to whom honor.

Romans 13:1 · Romans 13:6–7

Also taught in: 1 Peter 2:13–17 · Titus 3:1
The word of Christ: To give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s

51. We must obey God rather than human beings.

Peter and the apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than human beings.

Acts 5:29

Also taught in: Acts 4:19–20
The word of Christ: To give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s · Not to fear those who kill the body; to fear Him who can destroy both soul and body

Suffering with Christ

52. Christ suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in His steps.

For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in His footsteps. He committed no sin, nor was deceit found in His mouth. When He was reviled, He did not revile in return; when He suffered, He did not threaten, but entrusted His cause to the One who judges justly.

Also taught in: Hebrews 5:5–6
Scripture and event: Melchizedek blesses Abraham, Genesis 14:18–20 · The oath of the Lord, Psalm 109 (110):4

102. Christ entered once for all into the holy places, not with the blood of goats and calves but with His own blood.

With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship. But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance. … But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation— and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption. For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the cleanness of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through an eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!

Hebrews 9:6–7 · Hebrews 9:11–14

Scripture and event: The Day of Atonement, Leviticus 16:15–16 · Once a year, Leviticus 16:34 · The red heifer, Numbers 19:2–9

103. It is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins: a body You prepared for Me.

for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins. Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me. In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin You took no pleasure. Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Your will, O God.’” After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin You did not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law— He then said, “Look, I have come to do Your will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second. By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

Hebrews 10:4–10

Scripture and event: Sacrifice You did not desire, Psalm 39 (40):7–9

104. Jesus suffered outside the gate; let us go out to Him outside the camp, bearing His reproach.

We have an altar from which those serving the tent have no authority to eat. For the bodies of those animals whose blood the high priest brings into the holy places for sin are burned outside the camp. Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the gate, so that He might sanctify the people through His own blood. So let us go out to Him outside the camp, bearing His reproach. For here we have no lasting city, but we seek the one to come.

Hebrews 13:10–14

Scripture and event: Burned outside the camp, Leviticus 16:27

105. He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree; by His wounds you were healed.

He Himself bore our sins in His body upon the tree, so that, having died to sins, we might live to righteousness. By His wound you were healed. For you were wandering like sheep, but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

1 Peter 2:24–25

Also taught in: Acts 8:32–35
Scripture and event: The suffering servant, Isaiah 53:4–7

106. The stone the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.

For it stands in Scripture: “Look, I am laying in Zion a stone, a chosen, precious cornerstone, and the one who believes in Him will certainly not be put to shame.” Therefore, the honor is for you who believe; but for those who do not believe, “The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner,” and “a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.” They stumble, disobeying the word; to this they were also appointed.

1 Peter 2:6–8

Also taught in: Acts 4:11 · Ephesians 2:20
Scripture and event: The rejected stone, Psalm 117 (118):22 · A stone laid in Zion, Isaiah 28:16 · Christ applies it to Himself, Matthew 21:42

107. David, being a prophet, foresaw and spoke of the resurrection of the Christ.

For David says concerning Him, ‘I kept the Lord before me always, for He is at my right hand so that I will not be shaken. Therefore my heart rejoiced and my tongue exulted; moreover, my flesh will dwell in hope, because You will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor allow Your Holy One to see decay. You have made known to me the paths of life; You will fill me with gladness in Your presence.’ Men, brothers, I may speak openly to you about the patriarch David: he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this day. Since he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn an oath to him to seat one of his descendants upon his throne, he foresaw and spoke about the resurrection of the Christ: He was neither abandoned to Hades, nor did His flesh see decay. …

Acts 2:25–32

Also taught in: Acts 13:35–37
Scripture and event: You will not abandon my soul to Hades, Psalm 15 (16):8–11

108. The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at My right hand.

Therefore, exalted to God’s right hand and having received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit, He has poured out this which you see and hear. For David did not ascend into the heavens, but he himself says, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”’ Therefore let the whole house of Israel know with certainty that God has made Him both Lord and Christ—this Jesus whom you crucified.”

Acts 2:33–36

Also taught in: Hebrews 1:13 · 1 Corinthians 15:25
Scripture and event: The oracle to David’s Lord, Psalm 109 (110):1 · Christ’s own question, Matthew 22:41–45

109. Moses said, The Lord God will raise up for you a prophet like me from your brothers; to Him you shall listen.

Moses said, ‘The Lord God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You shall listen to him in everything he says to you. Every person who does not listen to that prophet will be destroyed from among the people.’

Acts 3:22–23

Also taught in: Acts 7:37
Scripture and event: The prophet like Moses, Deuteronomy 18:15–19

110. This is what was spoken through the prophet Joel: I will pour out My Spirit upon all flesh.

Rather, this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel: ‘In the last days, God says, I will pour out My Spirit upon all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy; your young men will see visions, and your elders will dream dreams. Even upon My male slaves and My female slaves in those days I will pour out My Spirit, and they will prophesy. I will give wonders in heaven above and signs on the earth below: blood and fire and a cloud of smoke. The sun will be changed into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes. And everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.’

Acts 2:16–21

Also taught in: Romans 10:13
Scripture and event: The Spirit poured out, Joel 3:1–5

111. The council at Jerusalem: not to trouble the nations who turn to God, but to abstain from things polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from what is strangled, and from blood.

After they fell silent, James spoke: “Men, brothers, listen to me. Simeon has related how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people for His name. With this the words of the prophets agree, as it is written: ‘After these things I will return and rebuild David’s fallen tent. I will rebuild its ruins and set it upright, so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, and all the nations upon whom My name has been called, says the Lord, who makes these things known from long ago.’ Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from the Gentiles who are turning to God, but should write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, sexual immorality, what is strangled, and blood. … For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to place no further burden upon you except these necessary things: to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, blood, things strangled, and sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.”

Acts 15:13–20 · Acts 15:28–29

Scripture and event: The tent of David rebuilt, Amos 9:11–12 · Blood not to be eaten, Leviticus 17:10–14 · The command to Noah, Genesis 9:4

112. You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for His possession.

But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s possession, so that you may proclaim the excellences of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light. Once you were not a people, but now you are God’s people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.

1 Peter 2:9–10

Scripture and event: A kingdom of priests, Exodus 19:5–6 · Not My people made My people, Hosea 2:25

113. All flesh is like grass, but the word of the Lord remains forever.

For “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like a flower of grass. The grass withered, and the flower fell, but the word of the Lord remains forever.” And this is the word that was proclaimed to you as good news.

1 Peter 1:24–25

Also taught in: James 1:10–11
Scripture and event: The grass withers, Isaiah 40:6–8

114. We were eyewitnesses of His majesty when the voice came: This is My beloved Son.

For we did not follow cleverly devised myths when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we became eyewitnesses of His majesty. For He received honor and glory from God the Father when a voice such as this was borne to Him by the Majestic Glory: “This is My Son, My Beloved, in whom I have taken pleasure”— and we ourselves heard this voice borne from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain. And we have the prophetic word more firmly established, to which you do well to pay attention as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts,

2 Peter 1:16–19

Scripture and event: The Transfiguration, Matthew 17:1–5

Wisdom for the Household of God

115. Whom the Lord loves He disciplines; endure it as sons.

and you have forgotten the encouragement that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline, nor faint when reproved by Him. For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and scourges every son He receives.” Endure for discipline. God deals with you as sons; for what son is there whom a father does not discipline? But if you are without discipline, in which all have become partakers, then you are illegitimate children and not sons. Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh as disciplinarians and respected them. Shall we not much more submit to the Father of spirits and live? For they disciplined us for a few days according to what seemed right to them, but He for our benefit, so that we may share in His holiness. …

Hebrews 12:5–11

Scripture and event: My son, do not despise the Lord’s discipline, Proverbs 3:11–12

116. God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.

But He gives greater grace. Therefore it says, “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.” Submit yourselves therefore to God; but resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

James 4:6–7

Also taught in: 1 Peter 5:5
Scripture and event: Grace to the humble, Proverbs 3:34

117. If your enemy is hungry, feed him; for by doing this you will heap burning coals upon his head.

But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head.

Romans 12:20

Scripture and event: Bread for the enemy, Proverbs 25:21–22

118. Whoever desires to love life and see good days, let him keep his tongue from evil and seek peace.

For “The one who wishes to love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit. He must turn away from evil and do good; he must seek peace and pursue it. For the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears attend to their petition, but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”

1 Peter 3:10–12

Scripture and event: Who is the man who desires life, Psalm 33 (34):13–17

119. Be angry and do not sin.

Be angry and do not sin. Do not let the sun go down upon your anger,

Ephesians 4:26

Scripture and event: Be angry and do not sin, Psalm 4:5

120. With the Lord one day is as a thousand years: He is patient, not wishing any to perish.

But do not let this one thing escape you, beloved: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day. The Lord is not slow concerning the promise, as some consider slowness, but is patient toward you, not wishing anyone to perish but all to come to repentance.

2 Peter 3:8–9

Scripture and event: A thousand years in Your sight, Psalm 89 (90):4

121. There is none righteous, not even one; all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.

What, then? Are we better off? Not at all; for we have already charged both Jews and Greeks with all being under sin, just as it is written: “There is no righteous one, not even one; there is no one who understands; there is no one who seeks God. All turned aside; together they became useless. There is no one who does kindness; there is not even one. … for all sinned and fall short of God’s glory, being justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,

Romans 3:9–12 · Romans 3:23–24

Scripture and event: None who does good, Psalm 13 (14):1–3

122. If anyone is not willing to work, let him not eat; and do not grow weary in doing good.

For even when we were with you, we gave you this command: if anyone is not willing to work, neither let him eat. For we hear that some among you are walking disorderly, not working at all but working at everyone else’s business. Now such people we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ to work quietly and eat their own bread. But you, brothers, do not lose heart in doing good.

2 Thessalonians 3:10–13

Also taught in: 1 Thessalonians 4:11–12 · Ephesians 4:28
Scripture and event: By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread, Genesis 3:19

123. Let marriage be held in honor; be content with what you have, for He has said, I will never leave you.

Let marriage be honored among all, and the marriage bed undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers. Let your manner of life be free from the love of money, being content with what is present; for He Himself has said, “I will certainly not leave you, nor will I ever forsake you.” So we may say with confidence, “The Lord is my helper; I will not fear. What will a human being do to me?”

Hebrews 13:4–6

Scripture and event: I will not forsake you, Deuteronomy 31:6 · The Lord is my helper, Psalm 117 (118):6

124. Adam was formed first, then Eve: the apostle’s order for teaching in the assembly.

Let a woman learn in quietness, in all submission. But I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man, but to be in quietness. For Adam was formed first, then Eve, and Adam was not deceived, but the woman, being deceived, came to be in transgression. But she will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith and love and sanctification with self-restraint.

1 Timothy 2:11–15

Also taught in: 1 Corinthians 11:8–12
Scripture and event: The woman made from the man, Genesis 2:21–23 · The deception, Genesis 3:13
